cases.candidate_question: Is every finitely generated module over every commutative ring Noetherian?
cases.mathematical_reason: Let R=k[x₁,x₂,…] and M=R. M is cyclic over R, but the strictly ascending ideals (x₁)⊊(x₁,x₂)⊊… show that it is not Noetherian. Finite generation of M cannot replace Noetherianity of R.

cases.candidate_question: If M/U is Noetherian, must M be Noetherian without a condition on U?
cases.mathematical_reason: Take an infinite-dimensional vector space M over a field and U=M. M/U=0 is Noetherian, whereas M is not. The exact pair M→M→0 with identity then zero also shows why the first endpoint assumption cannot be dropped.

cases.candidate_question: If M/U is Artinian, must M be Artinian without a condition on U?
cases.mathematical_reason: Take M=Z as a Z-module and U=M. M/U=0 is Artinian but M has the strictly descending submodules 2ⁿZ. The exact pair Z→Z→0 has Artinian final endpoint but non-Artinian middle module.

cases.candidate_question: Can the finite-product chain-condition theorems be applied to arbitrary infinite products?
cases.mathematical_reason: Let V be the product of countably many copies of a field k. The spans of the first n standard basis vectors form a strictly ascending submodule chain. The subspaces of sequences whose first n coordinates vanish form a strictly descending chain. Thus V is neither Noetherian nor Artinian although every factor is both.

cases.candidate_question: Is every injective endomorphism of a Noetherian module surjective?
cases.mathematical_reason: Multiplication by 2 on the Noetherian Z-module Z is injective and is not surjective. The card assumes surjectivity and concludes injectivity, in the opposite direction.

cases.candidate_question: Is every surjective linear endomorphism of an arbitrary module injective?
cases.mathematical_reason: On the direct sum of countably many copies of a field, the left shift sends e₀ to 0 and eₙ₊₁ to eₙ. It is surjective with nonzero kernel. This module is not Noetherian.

cases.candidate_question: Is every injective endomorphism of an arbitrary module surjective?
cases.mathematical_reason: Multiplication by 2 on Z is injective and not surjective. Z is not an Artinian Z-module, as the descending chain 2ⁿZ demonstrates.

cases.candidate_question: If N is Noetherian, is Hom_R(M,N) Noetherian for every M?
cases.mathematical_reason: Let R=k be a field, N=k and M=⊕ₙk. Then Hom_k(M,k)≅∏ₙk contains arbitrarily large independent finite families of coordinate functionals, so it is infinite-dimensional and not Noetherian. The source M is not finitely generated.

cases.candidate_question: Does Noetherianity alone imply finite composition length?
cases.mathematical_reason: Z as a Z-module is Noetherian, but its strictly descending chain 2ⁿZ means it is not Artinian and has no finite composition series. Both chain conditions are required.

cases.candidate_question: If S⁻¹f is injective, must f be injective?
cases.mathematical_reason: Take R=Z, S={2ⁿ:n≥0}, M=Z/2Z, N=0 and f=0. Both localized modules are zero, so S⁻¹f is injective, while f has nonzero kernel. Localization preserves injectivity but need not reflect it.

cases.candidate_question: If S⁻¹f is surjective, must f be surjective?
cases.mathematical_reason: For R=Z and S={2ⁿ:n≥0}, multiplication by 2 on Z becomes bijective after localization at S, but its original range is 2Z and it is not surjective onto Z.

cases.candidate_question: Are all canonical maps M→S⁻¹M injective, since localization is functorial?
cases.mathematical_reason: For R=Z, S={2ⁿ:n≥0}, and M=Z/2Z, the localized module is zero. The canonical map kills all of M. Naturality and preservation of composition do not assert injectivity of the canonical map.

cases.candidate_question: Does the localized submodule S⁻¹U always equal the image of U under M→S⁻¹M?
cases.mathematical_reason: Let R=M=Z, U=Z, S={2ⁿ:n≥0}. The image is Z inside Z[1/2], whereas the localized submodule is all of Z[1/2], including 1/2. With I=R the ideal-action equality does not remove this distinction.

cases.candidate_question: Does localization preserve arbitrary infinite intersections of submodules?
cases.mathematical_reason: Take R=M=Z, S={2ⁿ:n≥0} and Uₙ=2ⁿZ. Their intersection is zero and remains zero after localization. Each S⁻¹Uₙ is the whole Z[1/2], so the intersection of the localized submodules is nonzero. The card only asserts preservation of binary intersections.

cases.candidate_question: If M is Noetherian over R, is S⁻¹M necessarily Noetherian as an R-module?
cases.mathematical_reason: Take R=M=Z and S=Z\{0}. The localization Q contains the strictly ascending Z-submodules Z⊊(1/2)Z⊊(1/4)Z⊊…. Q is Noetherian over its localized ring Q but not over the original ring Z. The profile explicitly regards localized carriers as R-modules.

cases.candidate_question: Does tensoring with any X preserve every exact pair M→N→P without assuming the second map surjective?
cases.mathematical_reason: The pair 0→Z→Z, with the second map multiplication by 2, is exact at the middle Z. Tensor with X=Z/2Z: the resulting pair is 0→Z/2Z→Z/2Z with zero second map. Its middle kernel is all Z/2Z and the first image is zero. Thus it is not exact.

cases.candidate_question: Does every arbitrary function M×N→P have a linear tensor factorization?
cases.mathematical_reason: Over R=Z with M=N=P=Z, the constant function b(x,y)=1 cannot arise from any linear map out of M⊗N, because a linear map sends 0⊗0=0 to 0. Bilinearity is essential before the universal property or its naturality applies.

cases.candidate_question: Can a tensor-factor permutation or reassociation be replaced by a literal identity without transporting carriers?
cases.mathematical_reason: The canonical symmetry is a map M⊗N→N⊗M, and associativity has source (M⊗N)⊗P and target M⊗(N⊗P). These are different constructed carrier expressions in this typed language. Even when M=N=k², symmetry is not the identity: e₁⊗e₂ and e₂⊗e₁ are distinct basis tensors. Bijectivity does not authorize equating distinct typed carriers.

cases.candidate_question: Does contravariant Hom preserve exactness of any exact pair without the terminal map being surjective?
cases.mathematical_reason: Over Z the pair 0→Z→Z with multiplication by 2 as the second map is exact at the middle term. Applying Hom_Z(-,Z) gives Z→Z→0 with first map multiplication by 2; its image 2Z is strictly smaller than the kernel Z of the zero map. The missing surjectivity is essential.

cases.candidate_question: Does postcomposition by every surjective map induce a surjection on Hom_R(X,-)?
cases.mathematical_reason: For R=Z, X=Z/2Z and the surjection Z→Z/2Z, Hom_Z(X,Z)=0 whereas Hom_Z(X,Z/2Z) contains the identity. Postcomposition is not surjective. The card preserves injectivity, not arbitrary surjectivity.

cases.candidate_question: If f:M→N is injective, must precomposition Hom_R(N,X)→Hom_R(M,X) be injective?
cases.mathematical_reason: Take M=0, N=X=Z and the inclusion f:0→Z. The induced map Hom_Z(Z,Z)→Hom_Z(0,Z)=0 kills every endomorphism, including the identity. Surjectivity of f is the required assumption.
